subject: Aurora dedicated: GPU SKU selection checklist & fallback plan
content:
From: Sarah Collins <sarah@auroraanalytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — memory vs latency for long-context retriever workload

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. As discussed, we're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for our retrieval-augmented generation pipeline. High level:
- Peak concurrent users: ~1200 sessions, typical request sizes 1–3 queries, average context window ~50k tokens (longer docs).
- Token-generation pattern: 70% short replies (~50 tokens), 30% long summarizations (500–2,000 tokens).
- Hard latency target: p95 < 400ms for the short path, best-effort for long summarizations.

Attached is our workload_profile.csv with real distributions. Primary question: which GPU SKU should we reserve for Dedicated — H100, A100, or L4 — considering memory needs for large KV caches and cost? Also curious about fallback strategies if reserved capacity saturates.

Can you recommend a shortlist and next steps to get a sizing + pricing proforma?

Best,
Sarah
Director, Platform Engineering
Aurora Analytics

Attachment: workload_profile.csv (CSV, 12KB)

------------------------------------------------------------------

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Collins <sarah@auroraanalytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — memory vs latency for long-context retriever workload

Hi Sarah — thanks for the profile, looks helpful. Quick summary before we dig into numbers:
- Short path latency depends heavily on KV cache hit-rate and batching; for p95 < 400ms we typically recommend lower-batch, higher-frequency backends (H100s or L4s depending on model).
- Long-context summarization is memory-bound; if you plan to keep large KV caches per user/session, H100 (80GB) or an A100 80GB variant is likely necessary. L4s are attractive for cost but have smaller memory footprints.

I'm looping in Dev to run a quick SKU-fit pass and produce a simple matrix (latency/cost/memory) + fallback options. Ben — I'll need your help to give an estimated reserved-commit tier once we pick a target SKU.

Next step: Dev, can you run two sizing scenarios (optimistic cache hit-rate 60%; conservative 20%) and output a recommended mix and a canary plan? Aim to include: per-unit throughput (rps for short path), cost per 1M tokens, and the number of GPUs for 99% coverage of peak.

Mina
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora — initial SKU-fit matrix (H100 / A100 / L4)

Mina / Ben — attached is the SKU-fit matrix (sku-fit-matrix.xlsx). Summary of findings below. Numbers are rough but capture major tradeoffs.

Assumptions (taken from workload_profile.csv):
- Peak concurrent sessions: 1,200
- Avg short token generation: 50 tokens (p95 target)
- Avg long generation: 1,000 tokens (best-effort)
- KV cache per active session (conservative): 40GB; optimistic reuse: 10GB

SKU comparisons (high level):
- H100 (80GB, tensor cores optimized):
  - Memory: 80GB per card — best for per-session KV caches without sharding.
  - Latency: best for long-context single-session throughput; supports larger batch before hitting latency SLOs.
  - Cost: highest per-hour; fewer cards needed vs L4 for long jobs.
  - When to pick: if you must pin large KV caches per session and avoid cache sharding.

- A100 80GB (if available):
  - Memory: 80GB similar to H100; slightly older kernel support, throughput per card somewhat lower for newer transformer ops.
  - Latency: modestly slower than H100 on newer attention kernels; still good for memory-heavy workloads.
  - Cost: between H100 and L4 in practice (depends on procurement).

- L4 (48GB or 32GB options depending on cloud):
  - Memory: smaller, requires cache sharding or off-device KV store for 50k-token contexts.
  - Latency: very good for many short requests due to fast attention kernels for quantized models; cheaper per-hour so useful for scale-out.
  - When to pick: if workload has very high cache reuse (>60%) and you can accept sharding or external KV with mild extra latency.

Sizing scenarios (key outputs):
- Conservative (20% cache hit):
  - H100: 20 cards -> covers short-path p95 and gives headroom for long-summary concurrency; cost est in proforma attached.
  - A100: 24 cards -> similar memory but lower throughput -> slightly more units.
  - L4: 45 cards + external KV cluster -> much higher unit count, higher inter-node traffic, higher orchestration overhead.

- Optimistic (60% cache hit):
  - H100: 9 cards
  - A100: 11 cards
  - L4: 22 cards + local shard manager

Fallback strategies (recommended):
1) Region/fallback routing: route excess short-path requests to a cheaper L4 pool (stateless models) while prioritizing H100s for long-context jobs.
2) Autoscaling burst capacity: set an automated burst policy to spin up pre-warmed L4s when short-path latency rises; enforce throttles for long summaries.
3) Hybrid cache model: keep hot prefixes/kvs on-card (H100) and cold segments in a fast distributed KV (Redis or specialized KV store) so long-context jobs can be served with graceful degradation.

Attachments: sku-fit-matrix.xlsx (contains per-GPU rps, token cost estimates, and a simple cost proforma).

Dev
Senior Inferencing Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Aurora dedicated: GPU SKU selection checklist & fallback plan

Sarah / Team — thanks for the context. Pricing note: we can structure a two-phased reserved commit. For a pilot canary (4–8 weeks) we typically recommend a 4–6 card commit (H100 preferred if you want to validate long-context behavior) with monthly true-ups. For longer-term reserved pricing: 12–18 month commit tiers start to show material discounts (15–30% depending on commit size and SKU).

Action items for commercial proforma:
- Provide preferred SKU (H100/A100/L4) and target commit band (4–10 / 11–25 / 26+).
- We'll produce a price sheet with on-demand vs reserved and an estimate of token unit economics based on Dev's matrix.

I attached a preliminary cost proforma (aurora_cost_proforma.pdf) with ballpark numbers using Dev's conservative sizing.

Ben
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora dedicated: GPU SKU selection checklist & fallback plan

Thanks — this is very helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from our infra lead:
- If we go H100, can you quantify how much of the 80GB we realistically need per active session vs shard? We'd like to avoid a 1:1 mapping but also avoid excessive network hop for cold segments.
- For the L4 fallback, what does the expected p95 delta look like if we move short-path traffic to L4s (given quantized models)?

We'd like to run a 2-week spike test — temporary L4s for short path, small H100 pool for long-context canary. Would Redwood manage the canary routing and fallbacks?

Best,
Sarah

------------------------------------------------------------------

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Collins <sarah@auroraanalytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora dedicated: GPU SKU selection checklist & fallback plan

Sarah — yes, we can run exactly that spike test and manage routing. Short answers:
- Per-session memory: in our experience you can often keep a hot prefix (~8–16GB) on-card per active session and push cold KV to a shared store (Redis or an NVMe-backed store). We recommend instrumenting cache-hit tracing during the spike so we can tune the split.
- p95 delta to L4: for quantized short-path models we've measured p95 increases of ~50–120ms in practice depending on model and batch size; often still within your 400ms SLO if batching is tuned conservatively. We'll confirm with a small canary run.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) Week 0: provision a canary: 2x H100 + 6x L4, basic telemetry + KV tracing (2 weeks).
2) Week 1–2: run synthetic and limited-prod traffic, capture p95, cache hit-rates, and token cost.
3) Week 3: review results and pick production commit band (we'll provide revised SKU counts for conservative/optimistic).
4) Weeks 4–6: if agreed, roll a reserved commit with monthly true-up and a canary/rollback policy in the contract.

I'll schedule a 30-minute call to finalize MAP and commit band. Ben — please prepare the two-tiered proforma (pilot and 12-month commit) using Dev's conservative numbers. Dev — can you also add a small column in sku-fit-matrix.xlsx showing expected p95 delta for the short-path when moving to L4 fallback?

Thanks — looking forward to getting Aurora started.

Mina
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference
